## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `area:records` · `pm:queue`. The synthesized detail page evaluates each group's `visibleWhen` with the form's evaluator

Triage: lands in `packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` ⇒ `domain:ui`; rationale: the form half already holds; the detail page is the one reader that skips the predicate.

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-05T02:02Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Why p2.** The record page shows a section its author gated off, so the form and the detail page disagree on the same record. The verifier confirmed it (VF2). It predates 17.6.0.
- **Not an access boundary.** `visibleWhen` is a display predicate. The gated fields are readable through the record API either way, so this is not a security card.
- **Direction.** `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` (about `:717`–`:729`) carries each group's predicate and evaluates it with the evaluator `plugin-form/src/fieldGroups.ts` already uses. One evaluator, not a second copy.

## Seat ruling on PR objectui#11641's open question 1: route B, the spec-legal `{ group }` reference. Patch round 1, file surface amended

`domain:ui` execution seat 1 @ objectui · `session_015W8GBu6sBiqus2L2xjMsAL` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-05T04:44Z. This answers the dev's `open_questions[0]` in report `5988206775`. ⛔ Not a decision card: the governing text below decides it, so the options that conflict with it are not options here.

**Governing text:**
- objectstack `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md`: "协议为基准:spec 与代码不一致默认改代码对齐;改协议单独立卡,⛔ 不作缺陷卡的选项" (the protocol is the baseline: when spec and code disagree, change the code to match; a protocol change is its own card and never an option on a defect card).
- `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0 `RecordDetailsProps.sections[]`, read by the seat in the installed `dist/ui/index.d.ts`: the entry is `$strict`. It declares `group` (a field-group key reference, #13855) and `fields: string[]`, and no `visibleWhen`. The dev's parse probe agrees: `unrecognized_keys [visibleWhen]`, with a control that parses.
- `deriveFieldGroupLayout`'s TSDoc in the same spec: the derived section carries the group's predicate "verbatim", and "the renderer's section-gating contract evaluates it".

**Reading of the three options:**
- **C** (an enumerated section carries `visibleWhen`, and the renderer honours a key the spec refuses) conflicts with the protocol. It does not land.
- **A** (the spec declares `visibleWhen` on the entry) changes the protocol. It is not an option on this defect card. Anyone who wants it files it on its own, in the spec lane.
- **B** conforms. Group-derived sections are emitted as the spec's own `{ group: KEY }` reference (with the declared presentation keys only). `record:details` resolves the reference against the object's `fieldGroups` and gates the section with the group's carried `visibleWhen`, using the form's evaluator, which this PR already uses. The renderer stops reading `visibleWhen` off an enumerated section.

**Patch round 1 asks:**
- Take route B, measured. Find every consumer of the synthesized sections (`buildDefaultPageSchema` / `deriveFieldGroupDetailSections` / `resolveDetailSections`) and keep each one working. Name them in the PR body.
- This also retires the off-spec rich field descriptors on grouped sections, the dev's class-b finding.
- The output shape of `buildDefaultPageSchema` changes for grouped objects, and it is public API. The changeset names that change and its migration line, graded by AGENTS.md §9.
- `Clause-②: yes` stays declared, and the at-tier contract review runs on the delivered head.
- Update the PR body's route and test sections.

**Claim file surface, amended:** plus `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` and `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` (the `createSeed` path in `anchors.ts`), each only if route B measurably needs it.

**`open_questions[1]` (the fault direction) is not decided here.** This PR keeps the detail page's verdict identical to the form's, as the card's ruling orders ("exactly as the form does"). The objectui form already failed open before this card. The gap between the spec `deriveFieldGroupLayout` TSDoc ("fail-closed") and ADR-0137 D3 is a cross-repo text question. It is carried to the seat's round report for the maintainer.

## ACCEPT (content): PR objectui#11641, head `aeddcd7`, after patch round 1 (route B). The contract review is still owed before landing

`domain:ui` execution seat 1 @ objectui · `session_015W8GBu6sBiqus2L2xjMsAL` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-05T05:46Z. Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main`, not against the report's prose (report `5988831078`). The seat's ruling is `5988275811`.

- **Route B, as ruled.** Each declared field group is emitted as the spec's own `{ group: KEY, columns }` reference: `buildDefaultPageSchema` / `buildDefaultTabs` / `buildDefaultDetails` / `resolveDetailSections`. The console default page writes `{ group: KEY, showBorder: true }`. `record:details` resolves the reference and gates it with the form's evaluator (`resolveFieldRuleState` under `usePredicateScope`), failing open like the form. It no longer reads `visibleWhen` off an enumerated section. The `visibleWhen` key is gone from every emitted section.
- **Spec legality is pinned with controls.** On installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.6.0, `RecordDetailsProps.safeParse` accepts the synthesized grouped node. On the same parser, an enumerated section with `visibleWhen` is refused (`unrecognized_keys`), and so is one with a field object (`invalid_type`). That retires the dev's round-0 class-b finding, the off-spec rich descriptors on grouped sections.
- **The file surface stayed inside the amendment.** `RecordDetailView.tsx` was measurably needed, because its enumerated copies could not carry the predicate. The `createSeed` path needed no change. `plugin-detail/src/index.tsx` changes only the `record:details` registration's `sections` input description, prose on the renderer's own registration, and the changeset names it.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence.** It is `@object-ui/plugin-detail: minor` and `@object-ui/app-shell: minor`, with the output-shape break stated and graded `minor` under objectui's release model (no `major`). The "Unchanged" bullet is true: `deriveFieldGroupDetailSections` returns what it did, and no type member, zod member, registered input, prop or i18n key is added. Both migration lines match the diff.
- **Tests.** The parity matrix is now fed `{ group }` references, and the form, detail and expected verdicts agree. Ablation: dropping the gate turns 8 rows red, emitting the old copy 9, and reading `visibleWhen` off an enumerated section 1. Each restore was proven. The full `plugin-detail` and `app-shell` suites are green on `75c794c`. Only type annotations changed after that, and the app-shell type-check, lint and consumer pins were rerun green on `aeddcd7`.
- **Live before/after: NOT MEASURED.** The blocker is stated: the verify lock was saturated, and there was no built CLI in the shared checkout. The dispatch allowed that. The parity matrix is the evidence.
- **Shape.** The PR is a draft against `main`, and its assignee is `os-steve`. Its first line is `Fixes #11630`, the only line with a closing keyword next to an issue number. `Clause-②: yes` is on its own line.

**Owed before landing:** an isolated review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head. `needs:contract-review` is added to the PR in this stroke. **Carried to the maintainer, not decided here:** the fault direction of section predicates. The spec `deriveFieldGroupLayout` TSDoc says "fail-closed", while ADR-0137 D3, the form and now the detail page fail open.
